Job Overview:
T-Mobile Cloud is looking for a Member of Technical Staff (MTS) Hardware Engineer who will oversee the hardware design and integration of server racks from Original Design Manufacturers (ODMs). This position will work closely with our internal customers to understand their workloads and applications needs to provide a reliable hardware server solution. This role will be the technical decision maker for product management, system architecture, and engineering for the hardware design of the Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning (AI/ML), networking, compute, and storage rack infrastructure.
This experienced MTS Hardware Engineer is a visionary who possesses the technological acumen needed to translate the vision into a roadmap and communicate how the roadmap translates into product development. The applicant will have experience in delivering new product introduction (NPI) and product launches.
The candidate for this position will possess robust technical skills and is adept at navigating a rapidly evolving environment characterized by substantial ambiguity. The candidate will bring extensive experience in the enterprise hardware rack and server architecture, coupled with a proven track record of collaborating with cross-functional teams to deliver exceptional reliability at an optimal cost.
The position will own the end-to-end hardware design strategy, in-rack power, and thermal, and safety requirements. They make recommendations for new products and overall hardware architecture approach by partnering with senior level engineers that will run their workloads and applications on the cloud hardware.
This position will lead the transformation of our on-premises rack and server infrastructure, driving innovation and delivering cutting-edge solutions to meet the evolving needs of our customers and the telecommunications industry.

Job Responsibilities:

Responsibilities:
• Lead the technical design and implementation of large-scale, cross-platform cloud hardware solutions to optimize infrastructure performance and reliability.
• Develop and drive the technology roadmap for cloud hardware, ensuring alignment with organizational goals and industry best practices.
• Collaborate with senior engineers and cross-functional teams to evaluate and integrate new hardware products and architectural approaches.
• Mentor and guide engineers in technical development, fostering a culture of innovation and continuous improvement.
• Conduct signal integrity analysis, and manage CPU, memory, peripheral interfaces, and device firmware interactions to ensure robust system performance.
• Oversee the quality and reliability of third-party hardware suppliers, working closely with the supply chain to maintain high standards.
• Analyze competitive market and industry trends to identify opportunities for innovation and strategic advantage.
• Serve as the technical spokesperson for rack and server engineering, representing T-Mobile's technical capabilities.

Qualifications:
• 7-10 years related work experience (Required)
• 5+ years developing cloud server and rack hardware solutions (Required)
• 5+ years as lead technologist, architect engineer in the hardware space for a major technology, component, product, product line
• Experience with memory, CPU, signal integrity, peripheral device integration, hardware monitoring sensors, and device firmware interaction (Required)
• Experience as a lead engineer for complex electronic systems (Required)
• Experience driving the technology roadmap and quality of third-party suppliers and working with supply chain (Required)
• Experience with mentoring engineers on technical development (Required)
• Experience with in-rack power, cooling, and thermal solutions (fans, heatsinks, liquid cooling, power supply units, inverters, and batteries) (Preferred)
• Experience with statistical analysis and modeling for reliability, performance, and cost (Preferred)
• Experience Printed Circuit Board Assembly (PCBA) board layout optimization (Preferred)
• Experience in driving hardware reliability through design enhancement and failure mode analysis (Preferred)
• Experience with data center deployments of compute related infrastructure (Preferred)
• Experience with the hardware development life cycle management (part library management, PLM); and bill of material (BOM) part numbering management (Preferred)

Education:
• Bachelor's Degree of Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, Mechanical Engineering, a related subject area, or equivalent industry experience (Required)
• Masters/PhD/Advanced Degree of Engineering, Computer Science, or a related subject area (Preferred)

Job Description

At Boeing, we innovate and collaborate to make the world a better place. We’re committed to fostering an environment for every teammate that’s welcoming, respectful and inclusive, with great opportunity for professional growth. Find your future with us.

The Boeing Company is currently seeking a Customer Relationship Management UX Specialist (Mid-Level or Senior) to join the team in Seattle, WA or Renton, WA.

As a CRM UX Specialist, you will spearhead user-centered design initiatives for our enterprise CRM platforms, primarily focusing on Salesforce and related tools. Your expertise will be instrumental in mapping user journeys, creating intuitive interfaces, and streamlining workflows for sales, marketing, service, and support teams. By conducting user research, usability testing, and accessibility reviews, you will continuously refine designs to meet user needs. Collaborating closely with product managers, developers, and business stakeholders, you will ensure our CRM solutions are engaging, accessible, and aligned with Boeing’s high standards. This pivotal role supports our digital transformation by delivering seamless, data-driven experiences across our CRM ecosystem.

Position Responsibilities:
• Lead user research activities—including interviews, surveys, and usability tests—to gather insights that drive design improvements
• Conduct accessibility assessments and usability evaluations to ensure CRM interfaces meet WCAG standards
• Develop comprehensive user flows and journey maps for diverse CRM personas, identifying pain points and designing targeted solutions
• Create wireframes, prototypes, and high-fidelity designs using tools like Figma and Adobe XD to develop intuitive, user-centric interfaces
• Collaborate with product managers, stakeholders, and technical teams to define requirements, prioritize features, and ensure smooth integration of UX solutions.
• Document UX strategies, design guidelines, and maintain a reusable design system to ensure consistency across platforms
• Apply responsive and accessible design standards, delivering optimal desktop and mobile experiences
• Partner with Information Technology (IT) and CRM administrators to support data flow, third-party integrations, and custom modules, ensuring user-friendly data interactions
• Mentor junior designers and promote UX best practices within cross-functional teams, fostering a user-centric culture
• Lead UX strategy and prototyping efforts across Salesforce clouds, supporting end-to-end release cycles, including post-deployment validation
• Utilize tools such as Figma, Adobe Creative Suite, and Copado for design, prototyping, and release readiness reviews
• Ensure designs align with Boeing’s branding, UI standards, and security protocols, integrating data security and user access considerations

Basic Qualifications (Required Skills/Experience):
• 3+ years of experience designing enterprise web or mobile applications, especially CRM systems (preferably Salesforce)
• 3+ years of experience with Salesforce Lightning, Flows, and CRM-specific UX workflows
• 3+ years of experience in user research, usability testing, and A/B testing methodologies
• 3+ years of experience with design and prototyping tools such as Figma, Adobe XD, or similar
• Experience working within Agile environments, utilizing tools like Azure DevOps, JIRA, etc.
• Experience with CI/CD pipelines and release management tools like Copado

Preferred Qualifications (Desired Skills/Experience):
• 5 or more years' related work experience or an equivalent combination of education and experience Salesforce UX Designer Certification
• Salesforce Administrator Certification
• Experience with Salesforce Experience Cloud (Communities), Mobile Publisher, or customized Lightning experiences
• Experience in data architecture, SSO integration, and security role mapping.
• Experience in regulated enterprise environments such as aerospace, manufacturing, or defense
• Experience with user-centered design solutions for complex business applications
• Experience in continuous improvement or lean workshops

Drug Free Workplace:

Boeing is a Drug Free Workplace where post offer applicants and employees are subject to testing for marijuana, cocaine, opioids, amphetamines, PCP, and alcohol when criteria is met as outlined in our policies.

Overview

At PNNL, our core capabilities are divided among major departments that we refer to as Directorates within the Lab, focused on a specific area of scientific research or other function, with its own leadership team and dedicated budget.

Our Science & Technology directorates include National Security, Earth and Biological Sciences, Physical and Computational Sciences, and Energy and Environment. In addition, we have an Environmental Molecular Sciences Laboratory, a Department of Energy, Office of Science user facility housed on the PNNL campus.

The National Security Directorate (NSD) drives science-based, mission-focused solutions to take on complex,?real-world?threats to our nation and the world.

The AI and Data Analytics Division, part of the National Security Directorate, combines profound domain expertise and creative integration of advanced hardware and software to deliver computational solutions that address complex data and analytic challenges. Working in multidisciplinary teams, we connect foundational research to engineering to operations, providing the tools to innovate quickly and field results faster. Our strengths are integrated across the data analytics lifecycle, from data acquisition and management to analysis and decision support.

Responsibilities

We are seeking a Level 1 Software Engineer with experience in integrating specialized hardware and software using Open Architecture design approaches, notably within transportation security systems. The ideal candidate will possess experience with the Open Platform Software Library (OPSL), automation of complex workflows, and collaboration within multidisciplinary teams.

Key Responsibilities:
• Integration: Contribute to the integration of specialized security screening hardware (e.g., PNNL Developed HD-AIT, Analogic CT, Sandia developed ATR) with analytic tools using Open Architecture standards.

• Development and Implementation: Collaborate on developing new detection algorithms, user interfaces, and reporting systems. Support the creation of simulations based on generative AI models for airport passenger flow.
• Standardization Compliance: Apply understanding of Digital Imaging and Communications Security (DICOS) standards to ensure the integration and connectivity of transportation security systems.
• Collaboration & Leadership: Participate actively in team projects, design sessions, architectural reviews, and pair programming.
• Initiative and Continuous Improvement: Proactively tackle ambiguous and complex integration tasks, working with oversight from senior engineers to ensure high-quality, collaborative solutions. Provide and seek constructive feedback to drive personal and team growth through PR reviews and pair programming sessions.

Technical Skills Required:
• Familiarity with Open Architecture design principles
• Experience in OPSL
• Strong programming skills in C++ and Python
• Understanding of database management concepts using PostGres SQL
• Familiarity with Open Search
• Knowledge of AWS Native Services
• Experience in API Development and Data Engineering
• Knowledge of DevOps and DevSecOps methodologies

This position is based at the PNNL main campus in Richland, WA and requires onsite work.

Pacific Northwest National Laboratory (PNNL) is a world-class research institution powered by a highly educated, diverse workforce committed to the values of Integrity, Creativity, Collaboration, Impact, and Courage. job_title: Assistant Director of Technology Services Division (IT Policy & Planning – Senior Manager)
job_description:
Description

About WSDOT

The Washington State Department of Transportation (WSDOT) is a multimodal agency with a global reputation for excellence. Our dedicated workforce plans, designs, builds, and operates an integrated transportation system that safely and efficiently moves people and goods throughout the state. In addition to maintaining over 20,000 lane miles of state highway and 4,100 bridges, WSDOT manages the world's longest floating bridge, leads an award-winning Active Transportation Plan, holds the record for the world’s widest tunneling project, and operates the largest ferry system in the nation!

The Opportunity

WSDOT is currently seeking a senior manager to serve as an Assistant Director for the Technology Services Division (AD TSD). In this role, you will be responsible for the technological activities and decisions that support the business mission of WSDOT. This position reports to the Director of TSD and has a dotted line reporting relationship to the Deputy Secretary of WSDOT, Washington State Ferries (WSF). This position is responsible for strategic technology planning activities related to WSF operations including the development of formal and informal service-level agreements, budgeting, and participating in the technical review, change management, and standards development activities of TSD. These responsibilities are carried out in support of WSF operations and under the direction and guidance of the WSDOT CIO & Director of TSD. The successful candidate will serve as one of six ADs assigned to the WSDOT TSD. Each AD is assigned to a specific role and service area within TSD but works collaboratively as part of the TSD executive leadership team to ensure enterprise services levels and support across all agency lines of business. ADs are recruited and hired to lead a specific area of TSD (such as in support of WSF operations) but are expected to be experience technology executive leaders that can be assigned to other AD leadership roles in one of the other five TSD sections by the agency CIO if/when needed.

What to Expect

The WSDOT TSD Ferries team functions as the central support department for all technology-related equipment, software, and systems for the nearly 1,800 employees working for WSF. This includes 20 terminals and 21 vessels spanning seven counties, two countries, three major WSF facilities, and four commercial shipyards. Specifically, TSD Ferries is responsible for the management of end-user computing devices, workstations, tablets, servers, storage, data networks, cloud resources, point-of-sale devices, printers, mobile devices, telecommunications systems, cell phones, copiers, etc., administration of services, WSF-specific applications, and maintaining the working condition of all physical security equipment. These responsibilities are critical so that WSF staff can complete their assigned work activities and keep WSF facilities operating safely and securely.

Among the varied range of responsibilities held within this role, the Assistant Director of Technology Services Division will:
• Manage all TSD responsibilities in support of the WSF Division.
• Participate in strategic and operational governance of WSF as a representative of TSD and delegate of the WSDOT CIO, serving as a member of the WSF executive leadership team.
• Develop a supporting technology services strategic and operational plan.
• Manage and oversee Technology Services projects that impact the safety, security, and operations within WSF.
• Provide operational oversight of the TSD Ferries operations including workstation, physical security, revenue systems, ferry applications, and infrastructure.
• Lead staff by communicating job expectations; planning, monitoring, and appraising job results; coaching, counseling, and disciplining employees as needed; initiating, coordinating, and enforcing policies, processes, and procedures.
• Participate as a member of WSDOT’s strategic planning team in developing and implementing the agency’s strategic plan, policies, standards, and guidelines.
• Ensure new applications and enhancements will meet current industry standards and meet standards and policies in conjunction with WSDOT objectives and strategies.
• Participate with TSD peer Assistant Directors to develop and plan implementation of technology strategies, policies, standards, and guidelines for overall management of TS resources at WSF and the agency.
• Manage the Ferries Technology Services Organization Budget.

Qualifications

To be considered for this opportunity, the following are required:
• Eight (8) years of experience in a Technology Services leadership role OR a bachelor’s degree in computer science, computer engineering, or related Information Technology field and six (6) years of experience in a Technology Services leadership role.
• Knowledge of Technology Services strategic planning, consulting, and deployment strategies.
• Knowledge of current technology innovations and methods; feasibility studies; architecture standards.
• Experience preparing operational budgets.
• Experience with large, multi-agency projects.
• The ability to enhance Customer Relations, executive management communications, and to communicate technical information effectively to non-technical executives.
• Skills and experience with balancing and prioritizing workloads and ensuring adequate resources.
• Diverse team management skills.
• Experience promoting effective coordination between work groups.

It is preferred that qualified candidates also have:
• A master’s degree in business administration or equivalent.
• FEMA Incident Command System (ICS).
• CAPM or other Project Management Certification.
• LEAN 6 Sigma.
• Broad perspective of WSDOT goals, objectives, priorities, business plans and operations practices.
• State and WSDOT Technology Services policies, procedures, standards, and practices.

Overview

The Computing and Information Technology Directorate works to re-imagine how digital technologies can simplify the research experience, enable data-driven insights for decision makers, and accelerate PNNL’s research missions. CIT helps connect staff to systems while enabling a broader research computing ecosystem to improve productivity and provide a sense of community.

Responsibilities

Designs, develops, documents, tests, and debugs new and existing software systems, hardware/software interfaces, and/or applications according to industry established software engineering principals and best practices. Works collaboratively within a team to execute on the full system development lifecycle including analyzing user needs to determine technical requirements; developing technical specifications based on conceptual design and requirements; developing well-crafted and documented source code; integrating hardware using software; automating manual tasks; and consulting with the end user to prototype, configure, refine, test, and debug programs or systems to meet needs. Identifies and evaluates new technologies or methods for implementation and continuous improvement.

Applies engineering and technical principles to the design and development of computer networks, cyber security infrastructure, telecommunications, information technology systems and tools, and database systems. Analyzes, installs, integrates, modifies, and supports all associated systems, networks, software, and databases. Plans and conducts projects after analysis of functional and operational requirements. May consult with and lead cross-functional teams.

Key Responsibilities
• Design, develop, test, and maintain scalable software solutions using a variety of programming languages (e.g., Python, JavaScript, C#, etc.).
• Build and manage CI/CD pipelines for efficient code deployment using tools like GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps, or similar.
• Develop and manage APIs using Azure API Management (APIM) and deploy applications in Azure App Service Environments (ASE).
• Create low-code/no-code solutions using Microsoft Power Platform, including Power Apps, Power Automate (formerly Power Flow), and Copilot Studio.
• Contribute to AI-driven application development and integration of intelligent automation features.
• Advocate for and implement automation best practices across development and operational workflows.
• Take initiative in leading small-to-medium projects or product features in an agile/scrum environment.
• Collaborate cross-functionally with stakeholders, UX designers, business analysts, and cloud infrastructure teams.
• Ensure security, compliance, and performance optimization are integral to all development efforts.

• BS/BA or higher

Preferred Qualifications:
• Microsoft certifications (e.g., PL-400, AZ-204, AZ-400).
• Experience with AI integration, data workflows, or machine learning in business applications.
• Familiarity with containerization (e.g., Docker, Kubernetes) and infrastructure-as-code (e.g., Bicep, Terraform).

Not Applicable

• U.S. Citizenship
• Background Investigation: Applicants selected will be subject to a Federal background investigation and must meet eligibility requirements for access to classified matter in accordance with 10 CFR 710, Appendix B.

Note: Applicants will be considered ineligible for security clearance processing by the U.S. Department of Energy until non-use of illegal drugs, including marijuana, for 12 months can be demonstrated.

About PNNL

Pacific Northwest National Laboratory (PNNL) is a world-class research institution powered by a highly educated, diverse workforce committed to the values of Integrity, Creativity, Collaboration, Impact, and Courage. Every year, scores of dynamic, driven people come to PNNL to work with renowned researchers on meaningful science, innovations and outcomes for the U.S. Department of Energy and other sponsors; here is your chance to be one of them!

At PNNL, you will find an exciting research environment and excellent benefits including health insurance, and flexible work schedules. PNNL is located in eastern Washington State—the dry side of Washington known for its stellar outdoor recreation and affordable cost of living. The Lab’s campus is only a 45-minute flight (or ~3 hour drive) from Seattle or Portland, and is serviced by the convenient PSC airport, connected to 8 major hubs.

Our laboratory is committed to fostering a work environment where all individuals are treated with fairness and respect while solving critical challenges in fundamental sciences, national security, and energy resiliency. We are an Equal Employment Opportunity employer.

Pacific Northwest National Laboratory considers all applicants for employment without regard to race, religion, color, sex (including pregnancy, sexual orientation, and gender identity), national origin, age, disability, genetic information (including family medical history), protected veteran status, and any other status or characteristic protected by federal, state, and/or local laws.

We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations for individuals with disabilities and disabled veterans in our job application procedures and in employment. If you need assistance or an accommodation due to a disability, contact us at careers@pnnl.gov.

Drug Free Workplace

PNNL is committed to a drug-free workplace supported by Workplace Substance Abuse Program (WSAP) and complies with federal laws prohibiting the possession and use of illegal drugs.

If you are offered employment at PNNL, you must pass a drug test prior to commencing employment. PNNL complies with federal law regarding illegal drug use. Under federal law, marijuana remains an illegal drug. If you test positive for any illegal controlled substance, including marijuana, your offer of employment will be withdrawn.

Security, Credentialing, and Eligibility Requirements

In accordance with Homeland Security Presidential Directive 12 (HSPD-12) and Department of Energy (DOE) Order 473.1A, new employees are required to obtain and maintain a HSPD-12 Personal Identity Verification (PIV) Credential. This investigation includes a declaration of illegal drug activities, including use, supply, possession, or manufacture within the last year. The Help Desk Support Technician provides technical support to staff across the museum, ensuring smooth daily operations of hardware, software, and office equipment. Two years of information technology experience such as consulting, analyzing, installing, configuring and troubleshooting end user hardware and software; leading projects; providing customer or technical support in information technology.

More than Just a Paycheck!

Employee benefits are not just about the kind of services you get, they are also about how much you may have to pay out of pocket. Washington State offers one of the most competitive benefits packages in the nation.

We understand that your life revolves around more than just your career. Like everyone, your first priority is ensuring that you and your family will maintain health and financial security. That's why choice is a key component of our benefits package. We have a selection of health and retirement plans, paid leave, staff training and other compensation benefits that you can mix and match to meet your current and future needs.

Read About Our Benefits

The following information describes typical benefits available for full-time employees who are expected to work more than six months. Actual benefits may vary by appointment type or be prorated for other than full-time work (e.g. part-time); view the job posting for benefits details for job types other than full-time.

Note: If the position offers benefits which differ from the following, the job posting should include the specific benefits.

Insurance Benefits

Employees and their families are covered by medical (including vision), dental and basic life insurance. There are multiple medical plans with affordable monthly premiums that offer coverage throughout the state.

Staff are eligible to enroll each year in a medical flexible spending account which enables them to use tax-deferred dollars toward their health care expenses. Employees are also covered by basic life and long-term disability insurance, with the option to purchase additional coverage amounts.

To view premium rates, coverage choice in your area and how to enroll, please visit the Public Employees Benefits Board (PEBB) website. The Washington Wellness program from the Health Care Authority works with PEBB to support our workplace wellness programs.

Dependent care assistance allows the employee to save pre-tax dollars for a child or elder care expenses.

Other insurance coverage for auto, boat, home, and renter insurance is available through payroll deduction.

The Washington State Employee Assistance Program promotes the health and well-being of employees.

Retirement And Deferred Compensation

State Employees are members of the Washington Public Employees' Retirement System (PERS). New employees have the option of two employer contributed retirement programs. For additional information, check out the Department of Retirement Systems' web site.

Employees also have the ability to participate in the Deferred Compensation Program (DCP). This is a supplemental retirement savings program (similar to an IRA) that allows you control over the amount of pre-tax salary dollars you defer as well as the flexibility to choose between multiple investment options.

Social Security

All state employees are covered by the federal Social Security and Medicare systems. The state and the employee pay an equal amount into the system.

Public Service Loan Forgiveness

If you are employed by a government or not-for-profit organization, and meet the qualifying criteria, you may be eligible to receive student loan forgiveness under the Public Service Loan Forgiveness Program.

Holidays

Full-time and part-time employees are entitled to paid holidays and one paid personal holiday per calendar year.

Note: Employees who are members of certain Unions may be entitled to additional personal leave day(s), please refer to position specific Collective Bargaining Agreements for more information.

Full-time employees who work full monthly schedules qualify for holiday compensation if they are employed before the holiday and are in pay status for at least 80 nonovertime hours during the month of the holiday; or for the entire work shift preceding the holiday.

Part-time employees who are in pay status during the month of the holiday qualify for the holiday on a pro-rata basis. Compensation for holidays (including personal holiday) will be proportionate to the number of hours in pay status in the month to that required for full-time employment, excluding all holiday hours. Pay status includes hours worked and time on paid leave.

Sick Leave

Full-time employees earn eight hours of sick leave per month. Overtime eligible employees who are in pay status for less than 80 hours per month, earn a monthly proportionate to the number of hours in pay status, in the month to that required for full-time employment. Overtime exempt employees who are in pay status for less than 80 hours per month do not earn a monthly accrual of sick leave.

Sick leave accruals for part-time employees will be proportionate to the number of hours in pay status, in the month to that required for full-time employment. Pay status includes hours worked, time on paid leave and paid holiday.

Vacation (Annual Leave)

Full-time employees accrue vacation leave at the rates specified in WAC 357-31-165(1) or the applicable collective bargaining agreement (CBA). Full-time employees who are in pay status for less than 80 nonovertime hours in a month do not earn a monthly accrual of vacation leave.

Part-time employees accrue vacation leave hours in accordance with WAC 357-31-165(1) or the applicable collective bargaining agreement (CBA) on a pro rata basis. Vacation leave accrual will be proportionate to the number of hours in pay status, in the month to that required for full-time employment.

Pay status includes hours worked, time on paid leave and paid holiday.

As provided in WAC 357-58-175, an employer may authorize a lump-sum accrual of vacation leave or accelerate the vacation leave accrual rate to support the recruitment and/or retention of a candidate or employee for a Washington Management Service position. Vacation leave accrual rates may only be accelerated using the rates established WAC 357-31-165.

Note: Most agencies follow the civil service rules covering leave and holidays for exempt employees even though there is no requirement for them to do so. However, agencies are required to adhere to the applicable RCWs pertaining holidays and leave.

Military Leave

Washington State supports members of the armed forces with 21 days paid military leave per year.

Bereavement Leave

A GS-2210-12, IT SPEC (INFOSEC/NETWORK):
• Prepares for, maintains currency for, and executes an advanced role in Cyberspace Operations. Utilizes knowledge of systems security principles and concepts of emerging Information Technology (IT) security developments, and of the infrastructure protection environment to select appropriate tools to be used by team members.
• Establishes methodology and determines best techniques to secure computer systems and to protect cyber key terrain from exploitation of information within these systems and/or to achieve other tasked objectives in cyberspace.
• Leverages knowledge of multiple entities with a stake in current operations to plan and build appropriate courses of action and training scenarios. Functions in at least one of the following advanced roles:
• Cyberspace Crew Commander. Develops tactical objectives and/or tactical taskings for a team of Cyberspace Operators. Serves as the liaison between assigned team and other teams or external entities.
• Cyberspace Operations Controller. Directs tactical execution for a team of Cyberspace Operators. Develops tactical approach and synchronizes actions of multiple qualified operators in order to achieve objectives.
• Operations Planner/Scheduler. Represents the unit's capability, availability, and interests at high-level Operational Planning Team (OPT) meetings to define the mission, environment, enemy, effects, capabilities, overall plan, phasing, operational agreements and contingencies needed to conduct the operation or exercise. Develops a tactical plan for assigned missions and exercises. Works as a member of the mission leadership element to translate operational objectives into tactical objectives comprised of specific tactical tasks. Develops Measures of Effectiveness and Measures of Performance to be used in the assessment of the mission's or exercises success. Prepares and coordinates operator, resource, facilities and equipment schedules in coordination with unit and flight commanders in order to ensure training, currency, and mission timelines and objectives are met.
• Industrial Control Systems (ICS) Cyberspace Operator. Assesses and evaluates vulnerabilities and/or adversary activity in ICS enclaves. Detects, characterizes, and resolves insecurities in ICS networks. Reviews and analyzes ICS network traffic, configurations, and operating procedures and provides recommendations to improve system security posture.
• National Mission Team Cyberspace Operator. Maintains both Air Force currency and additional national-level requirements to execute US Cyber Command's Defend-the-Nation priority.
• Prepares Unit Training Assembly, Annual Training and currency training events for Mission Ready Cyberspace Operators to optimize training time available.
• Ensures training for each event has been prepared and is ready.
• Monitors assigned military members' go-no-go readiness status and ensures deficiencies are recognized.
• Works with scheduling section to provide opportunities for assigned members to maintain full mission readiness.
• Coordinates with maintenance section to ensure all assigned equipment is in good working condition and ready for each training and mission event.
• Conducts extensive research of new vulnerabilities and insecurities discovered in operating systems, application software, infrastructure and boundary protection devices.
• Investigates, analyzes, and develops methods that could be used to exploit these vulnerabilities.
• Conducts testing on training range to validate findings and to develop and refine methods and procedures to mitigate vulnerabilities.
• Coordinates research and findings with the Cyberspace Weapons Officer for inclusion in unit and cyberspace community tactics, techniques, and procedures.
• Conducts extensive research of tools currently being used to attack or gain unauthorized access to information networks.
• Analyzes and tests these tools on training range to determine effectiveness, stability, and scope of the tools.
• Recommends and refines tools for use on Cyberspace Weapon System to provide the customer with the best possible evaluation of their security posture.
• Other duties as assigned.

Position Description:

CGI Federal has an exciting opportunity for an Expert Cybersecurity Engineer within our Intel sector advancing the national security mission through cutting edge technology. You must have a passion for keeping pace with rapidly evolving cybersecurity advancements and leveraging your knowledge on a highly collaborative team to deliver state-of-the-art capabilities.

You will be responsible for leveraging deep subject matter knowledge and experience to lead matrixed teams of ISSOs and ISSEs to navigate the RMF process to achieve security authorization milestones for complex systems and applications while supporting security operations for deployed capabilities.

CGI Federal is growing its high-performance team whose members share a passion for building high-quality, scalable, advanced IT solutions in a collaborative, fast-paced, outcome-driven mission.

• Active TS/SCI with CI Poly

• A minimum of two years of experience relating to CS for Cloud or Hybrid Cloud environment.
• One or more ITIL certifications.
• Experience with implementation of DoD RMFs.
• IASAE certification.

Job Description

At Boeing, we innovate and collaborate to make the world a better place. We’re committed to fostering an environment for every teammate that’s welcoming, respectful and inclusive, with great opportunity for professional growth. Find your future with us.

The Boeing Company is looking for a highly experienced and detail-oriented Mid-Level Incident Response Specialist to join the team in Everett, WA; Renton, WA; Kent, WA; or Seattle, WA.

The Boeing Company has an exciting opportunity for an experienced Incident Response Specialist - eDiscovery and Computing Forensics - to join the Information Security Computing Forensics team in the Washington area.

The successful candidate will work in a fast-paced, high volume environment supporting attorneys, paralegals, and investigators across the enterprise by identifying, collecting, preserving, and analyzing responsive data and digital evidence. An ideal applicant will communicate effectively with technical and non-technical individuals as well as with all levels of management and third parties, work autonomy and as a team player and maintain extreme confidentiality in sensitive matters.

Position Responsibilities:
• Lead and/or perform eDiscovery collections and legally hold preservation activities in collaboration with The Boeing Law Department
• Supplement Information Security Computing Forensics incident response activities across broad and sometimes undefined technology profiles that can include multiple systems
• Determine incident scope, nature, technical mechanisms, personnel involvement, and business impact
• Identify incident path and method
• Collect and preserve evidence
• Perform event correlation and analysis
• Define and monitor time critical risk mitigation steps
• Draft, review, and deliver incident/investigation reports and make recommendations for future team and technical method process enhancements
• Provide testimony in administrative and criminal hearings
• Research and propose undefined technical response methods, tools and processes
• Assist management and end users with access to inaccessible data needed for business continuity purposes, audit assistance, and data spill containment

Basic Qualifications (Required Skills/Experience):
• 3+ years of experience with incident response
• Experience in a Cybersecurity Operations Center with monitoring and incident response

Preferred Qualifications (Desired Skills/Experience):
• Bachelor’s degree or higher
• Experience using eDiscovery and digital forensics tools beyond the classroom environment
• Experience with Electronic Discovery Reference Model (EDRM)
• Experience drafting technical findings reports based on network or system analysis to include incident path and user attribution
• Experience with tools that may include, but are not limited to enterprise eDiscovery
• Experience with applications, Sherpa Software’s Discovery Attender, AccessData’s Forensic Toolkit (FTK), XWays, Cellebrite, Magnet Forensics Axiom or Internet Evidence Finder (IEF), F-Response, hardware write blockers, Passware, Splunk, etc.
• Experience performing computer and/or network incident log analysis or computing related hardware and/or software investigations
• Certification in the field of eDiscovery and/or Computer Forensics and/or Information Security (i.e. Certified E-Discovery Specialist (CEDS), GIAC Certified Forensic Examiner (GCFE), GIAC Certified Forensic Analyst (GCFA), Certified Forensic Computer Examiner (CFCE), CISSP, Security+, etc.)

Analysis & Technical:
• Produces detailed documentation including business requirements, process flows, communications, use cases, and user stories outlining problems, and opportunities.

• Primary liaison with IT to support them in conducting more detailed investigations.

Description

Telemetry Systems Specialist (Chiller & Controls Technician)

Full-Time | Permanent

Union Represented | WFSE

Who We Are

The Department of Enterprise Services (DES) provides centralized business services to state government agencies; to other public entities such as cities, counties and tribes; and to Washington residents. DES’ mission is to strengthen the business of government for a sustainable and just future. Learn more about DES.

About The Division

The Buildings & Grounds Division (B&G) is responsible for the Capitol Campus and Department of Enterprise Services (DES) managed building operations, stewardship, and historic preservation. B&G provides service to over 42 agencies, maintains, operates and preserves the 486-acre state Capitol Campus in Olympia, including more than 28 buildings, 18 public monuments, over 6,000 parking stalls, four state parks and a 260-acre lake. B&G executes these responsibilities through the following service programs: Facilities Operations, Grounds Operations, Leadership and Admin, Maintenance & Repairs, Support Services (Custodial).

About The Position

The Telemetry Systems Specialist (Chiller & Controls Technician) is a lead position where the incumbent will be responsible for diagnosing higher level building automation control systems during the off season for – HVAC systems. You will perform maintenance and repairs for the Chiller Operation & Cooling Tower. This includes troubleshooting and correcting higher-level building automation systems that consist of chiller systems maintenance and controls as applied to HVAC/R and equipment.

This position reports to the HVAC/Controls Shop Supervisor. The selected incumbent will know how to analyze, operate, maintain, calibrate, repair and adjust various control systems and components as applied to HVAC, lighting and refrigeration equipment. Other duties entail operating, calibrating and maintaining electronic and analog testing as well as measuring instruments (digital analog and binary instrumentation, interfaces and communication), in addition to developing cost estimates, as well as attending planning and construction meetings.

This position reports directly to the assigned HVAC & Controls Shop Supervisor who works with the Quality Assurance and Planning Managers to schedule work and plans projects. You will interact with the Asset, Property and Tenant Facility Managers, B&G trade staff, building tenants, building automation team, vendors, contractors, and visitors. The Telemetry Systems Specialist is expected to work independently following all approved DES work processes and procedures; national and local building codes and standards to accomplish work assignments in a timely manner. You will spend time mostly indoors, with some work performed outside under adverse conditions. The work schedule is Monday – Friday, 40 hrs./week. Compressed work schedules are available upon request and approved by management.

Required

The Telemetry Systems Specialist is recognized as Continuity of Operations Plans (COOP) Designation – for Disaster or Emergency Recovery. This requires supporting any emergency situations that affect the DES owned properties, both on and off the Capital Campus. During a recognized emergency, duties may be different from normal duties and would be temporary in nature, lasting only as long as necessary to resume normal operations. You may be required to perform the following during a recognized emergency/disaster:
• Report for duty on short notice for the specified timeframe
• Report to duty outside of normally scheduled work hours and workdays
• Report to a duty station that is different from the official duty station
• Perform work tasks outside the normal scope of duties

For full details of this position, contact rachel.vaughan@deswa.gov and request to have the full job description emailed.

Duties

Some Of What You Will Be Doing

Diagnose Higher Level Building Automation Control Systems
• To analyze, operate, maintain, calibrate, repair and adjust various control systems and components as applied to HVAC, lighting and refrigeration equipment
• This position is the main point of contact for campus HVAC technicians to help better respond and understand the higher-level building automation control issue that arise
• Serve as lead technician for campus projects related to HVAC chillers and controls. Supports coordination and provide technical input to B&G Leadership, B&G Operations, and agency tenants

Chiller Operation and Cooling Tower, Maintenance and Repair
• Is the lead technician for operation, maintenance and repair of chiller and chiller related systems, both DES owned and chillers that are reimbursable customers to DES (these include but are not limited over 50 tons)
• Is the lead technician for operation, maintenance and repair of cooling tower and cooling tower related systems, both DES owned and cooling towers that are reimbursable customers to DES
• Work in depth with all aspects of the DES controls system (Metasys) and communicates with the other Controls Technicians to diagnose, troubleshoot and communicate with other Metasys operators on the higher-level function of the campus controls system

Develop cost estimates and attend planning and construction meetings
• Develop cost estimates of labor and materials needed for building maintenance, alteration, or remodeling projects
• Participate in planning and construction meetings and monitor the installation, repair and maintenance of chillers and chiller equipment when performed by others
• Read, interpret and update blueprints and as built drawings as needed
• Make technical recommendations as required or when requested

Qualifications

Required Qualifications
• Bachelor’s degree in computer science, electrical engineering, or closely allied field AND
• Two (2) years of experience in the design, installation, maintenance and repair of computerized telemetry systems OR
• An associate’s degree in electronics technology, computer science or closely allied field AND
• Four (4) years of experience in the design, installation, maintenance and repair of computerized telemetry systems
• *Additional qualifying experience may be substituted, year for year, for education**

Special Requirements In Addition To The Above Qualifications
• Possess and maintain a current EL-06A License issued by the Washington State Department of Labor and Industries
• Possess and maintain a current EPA universal refrigerant handling certification
• Possess and maintain a valid motor vehicle operator’s license, free from serious traffic violations

Preferred/Desired Qualifications
• Ability to perform skilled HVAC work and learn to fulfill the requirements of the chiller in training program
• Knowledge of standard practices, methods, materials, tools, and equipment used in the HVAC and chiller trade
• Knowledge of current HVAC, electrical codes and electrical safety precautions
• Ability to work from blueprints, plans and sketches; estimate labor and materials required to accomplish the work
• Use of hand and power tools required to accomplish HVAC work

AND

Incumbents to this position must possess and demonstrate the following DEI competencies:
• Able to learn and understand the language and concepts of our DES DEI culture and commit to being a part of creating and maintaining a diverse, equitable, respectful, and inclusive workplace
• Demonstrate a commitment to growth, learning and self-awareness when provided training and opportunities to participate in improving our work environment
• Participate and behave in a manner that creates trust and builds working relationships, promoting teamwork and collaboration in the work environment
• Demonstrate the understanding that all people are valued; contribute to an equitable, inclusive and respectful environment when working with members of the group, team, organization or community
• Commit to being an active participant in continually evaluating and improving strategies that promote equity and inclusion in our organization

More than Just a Paycheck!

Employee benefits are not just about the kind of services you get, they are also about how much you may have to pay out of pocket. Washington State offers one of the most competitive benefits packages in the nation.

We understand that your life revolves around more than just your career. Like everyone, your first priority is ensuring that you and your family will maintain health and financial security. That's why choice is a key component of our benefits package. We have a selection of health and retirement plans, paid leave, staff training and other compensation benefits that you can mix and match to meet your current and future needs.

Read About Our Benefits

The following information describes typical benefits available for full-time employees who are expected to work more than six months. Actual benefits may vary by appointment type or be prorated for other than full-time work (e.g. part-time); view the job posting for benefits details for job types other than full-time.

Note: If the position offers benefits which differ from the following, the job posting should include the specific benefits.

Insurance Benefits

Employees and their families are covered by medical (including vision), dental and basic life insurance. There are multiple medical plans with affordable monthly premiums that offer coverage throughout the state.

Staff are eligible to enroll each year in a medical flexible spending account which enables them to use tax-deferred dollars toward their health care expenses. Employees are also covered by basic life and long-term disability insurance, with the option to purchase additional coverage amounts.

To view premium rates, coverage choice in your area and how to enroll, please visit the Public Employees Benefits Board (PEBB) website. The Washington Wellness program from the Health Care Authority works with PEBB to support our workplace wellness programs.

Dependent care assistance allows the employee to save pre-tax dollars for a child or elder care expenses.

Other insurance coverage for auto, boat, home, and renter insurance is available through payroll deduction.

The Washington State Employee Assistance Program promotes the health and well-being of employees.

Retirement And Deferred Compensation

State Employees are members of the Washington Public Employees' Retirement System (PERS). New employees have the option of two employer contributed retirement programs. For additional information, check out the Department of Retirement Systems' web site.

Employees also have the ability to participate in the Deferred Compensation Program (DCP). This is a supplemental retirement savings program (similar to an IRA) that allows you control over the amount of pre-tax salary dollars you defer as well as the flexibility to choose between multiple investment options.

Social Security

All state employees are covered by the federal Social Security and Medicare systems. The state and the employee pay an equal amount into the system.

Public Service Loan Forgiveness

If you are employed by a government or not-for-profit organization, and meet the qualifying criteria, you may be eligible to receive student loan forgiveness under the Public Service Loan Forgiveness Program.

Holidays

Full-time and part-time employees are entitled to paid holidays and one paid personal holiday per calendar year.

Note: Employees who are members of certain Unions may be entitled to additional personal leave day(s), please refer to position specific Collective Bargaining Agreements for more information.

Full-time employees who work full monthly schedules qualify for holiday compensation if they are employed before the holiday and are in pay status for at least 80 nonovertime hours during the month of the holiday; or for the entire work shift preceding the holiday.

Part-time employees who are in pay status during the month of the holiday qualify for the holiday on a pro-rata basis. Compensation for holidays (including personal holiday) will be proportionate to the number of hours in pay status in the month to that required for full-time employment, excluding all holiday hours. Pay status includes hours worked and time on paid leave.

Sick Leave

Full-time employees earn eight hours of sick leave per month. Overtime eligible employees who are in pay status for less than 80 hours per month, earn a monthly proportionate to the number of hours in pay status, in the month to that required for full-time employment. Overtime exempt employees who are in pay status for less than 80 hours per month do not earn a monthly accrual of sick leave.

Sick leave accruals for part-time employees will be proportionate to the number of hours in pay status, in the month to that required for full-time employment. Pay status includes hours worked, time on paid leave and paid holiday.

Vacation (Annual Leave)

Full-time employees accrue vacation leave at the rates specified in WAC 357-31-165(1) or the applicable collective bargaining agreement (CBA). Full-time employees who are in pay status for less than 80 nonovertime hours in a month do not earn a monthly accrual of vacation leave.

Part-time employees accrue vacation leave hours in accordance with WAC 357-31-165(1) or the applicable collective bargaining agreement (CBA) on a pro rata basis. Vacation leave accrual will be proportionate to the number of hours in pay status, in the month to that required for full-time employment.

Pay status includes hours worked, time on paid leave and paid holiday.

As provided in WAC 357-58-175, an employer may authorize a lump-sum accrual of vacation leave or accelerate the vacation leave accrual rate to support the recruitment and/or retention of a candidate or employee for a Washington Management Service position. Vacation leave accrual rates may only be accelerated using the rates established WAC 357-31-165.

Note: Most agencies follow the civil service rules covering leave and holidays for exempt employees even though there is no requirement for them to do so. However, agencies are required to adhere to the applicable RCWs pertaining holidays and leave.

Military Leave

Washington State supports members of the armed forces with 21 days paid military leave per year.

Bereavement Leave

Most employees whose family member or household member dies, are entitled to three (3) days of paid bereavement leave. In addition, the employer may approve other available leave types for the purpose of bereavement leave.

Description

As an Operations Engineer, you will lead and manage the lifecycle of challenging cross-functional projects, developing and delivering the next generation of automation and material handling solutions. You are a customer obsessed leader that will play an integral part in planning and implementation of the facility network infrastructure including new builds, retrofits, expansions and program initiatives. Partnering with internal customers and internal/external stakeholders to engage as a team and ensure a timely handover will be part of your critical tasks.

As an Operations Engineer for Amazon, you will work with some of the most talented engineers in the design, development, and delivery of physical distribution systems around the globe. You are responsible for managing a technology or integration project, successfully delivering the solution to meet project goals. You may work directly with external equipment vendors, customers, or partners, and you have a solid understanding of the design approaches and industry technologies utilized in fulfillment and distribution center designs. To meet timelines and minimize disruption to support teams, you manage the overall schedule, proactively mitigate risks, and keep the scope of engineering deliverables under control.

Key job responsibilities
• Work independently with internal and external teams to successfully manage the lifecycle of challenging projects, and act as owner in delivering on project objectives and targets. Projects may span organizations or geographies in support of business objectives.
• Actively participate in firm engineering reviews, and make tangible impact on the proposed solutions on an individual system or its components, on the overall systems architecture, and on facility processes.
• Partner with internal teams, stakeholders and external vendors to set project priorities, establish milestones, and drive schedules to meet deadlines. Proactively assess stakeholders’ dependencies and milestones, problem-solve and drive solutions to mitigate the impact from the issues.
• Lead and coordinate all execution efforts in delivering systems and automated equipment designs per established standards and guidelines. Perform equipment/system installation, throughput and safety qualifications. Simplify, optimize, remove bottlenecks and provide feedback while resolving difficult system problems or technical deficiencies.
• Lead effective meetings by setting the objectives, putting the right people in the room and driving detailed business and technical discussions/alignment. Document meeting discussions, decisions and future steps, ensuring alignment on expectations with internal partner teams and outside vendors.
• Promptly and accurately communicate project status, risk analysis and risk mitigation plans. Effectively answer project questions in detail, and regularly produce clear and concise summaries for the project to leadership/management team.
• Competently articulate system and/or equipment designs, including layouts, technical specifications and functional capabilities to internal customers and partner teams.
• Support change order controls, purchase orders, and invoice validation/approvals.
• Excel at building strong working relationships with internal and external stakeholders across multiple projects.
• Identify and lead process improvement initiatives that improve the Engineering and cross-teams’ efficiencies, optimizing the teams’ value and delivery. Through collaboration, generate high-quality, cost-effective solutions in compressed periods of time.
• Travel 75% domestically although travel intensity can be variable and consist of up to three weeks in a row, including weekends.

Basic Qualifications
• Bachelor’s Degree in Industrial Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or other STEM field
• 4+ years of experience as a Project Engineer, Process Engineer, Project Manager, Manufacturing Engineer, or related occupation
• Experience managing the lifecycle of cross-functional projects, implementing automated equipment and/or integrated systems
• Experience with CAD software (AutoCAD, REVIT, BIM 360, etc.)
• Experience supporting deployment of new product/technology and/or large material handling and automation installations in a construction environment to include safety and permitting requirements.

Preferred Qualifications
• Master’s degree in Engineering, Operations, Business Administration, or a related STEM field
• Operations Management/Distribution Center experience with direct management or responsibility for material handling, automation, or other technical projects
• Experience with Six Sigma and/or Lean Manufacturing
• Experience with Microsoft Project, Smartsheet programs
• Experience with new product introduction and/or implementation automation solutions, such as Conveyors, Sorters, high speed manufacturing and packaging lines, Robotic work cells
• Proven technical leadership for industrial engineering projects or program

Want to join something GREAT and make a difference?
The Department of Natural Resources (DNR) has an exciting opportunity within our Southeast Region as a GIS Specialist. In this role, you will serve as the IT professional in application development and coding for the SE Region IT and GIS section, producing custom applications, extending the function of applications, implementing workflows when accuracy requirements are subjective or data involves many variables, and conducting research in collaboration with IT Division, other region GIS staff, Wildfire Management Division, and professional code resources. You will also assist the Forest Practices and Regulation Program by providing GIS support for the SE and NE Regions. You will provide mapping and geospatial support (extracting, transforming, and loading geospatial data) for the Forest Practices and Application Review System for environmental review. You also play a key role in supporting wildland fire management operations by providing timely and accurate spatial information about developing and ongoing incidents.Responsibilities:
• Provide guidance to management on the adoption of cutting-edge GIS technologies and modernization efforts that align with organizational goals.
• Foster collaboration, partner engagement, and staff development to enhance the Region’s GIS capabilities and ensure strategic alignment with organizational goals. This position is responsible for coordinating GIS activities across programs and prioritizing GIS workload effectively.
• Support the Region to develop, implement, and maintain critical systems that support business goals and initiatives. Program staff, management, partner agencies, and the public depend upon these complex geospatial information systems to accurately identify, examine, and reflect the conditions of the Region.
• Provide IT customer support to the Region staff. Assist in LAN, phone, and desktop support initiatives like infrastructure refreshes, service and network availability, business continuity, deployment of business-critical hardware and applications, and availability of business communication systems that may significantly impact Region operations and public services.
Required Qualifications:
• A Bachelor’s degree in information technology, computer sciences, or related field, with an emphasis in Geographic Information Systems, AND one year of relevant experience;
OR an equivalent combination of education and/or experience.
• Experience using geographic data and proficiency in database management.
• Experience in cartography and understanding map concepts.
• Experience in performing analysis and conveying data (spatial & tabular) to users in a meaningful format.
• Proficiency with the Python scripting language.
• Proficiency with various GPS devices and associated software, and experience providing GPS user support.
• Commitment to fostering and supporting an environment that honors diversity, equity, inclusion, and environmental justice practices.
• Perform assigned duties in a manner consistent with applicable laws, regulations, and public records retention and requests are followed.
• DNR Core Competencies:
• Personal Accountability
• Value Others
• Compassionate Communication
• Inspire Others
• Commitment to Excellence

Special Requirements and Conditions of Employment:
• This position’s assigned duty station is the region office. The work is performed in an office setting with occasional trips to the field as needed. The position does not come in contact with any hazardous chemicals other than standard surface cleaners, ink, and adhesives.
• This position requires occasional travel (5%) to field offices, field sites, and to attend out-of-office meetings
Desired Qualifications:
• Accustomed to innovative and forward-thinking in a fast-paced, changing technical environment.
• Experience working with, managing, and/or analyzing parcel GIS data.
• Knowledge of DNR programs and wildfire management principles (e.g., ICS, jurisdictional boundaries, interagency partners).
• Ability to Work Well in a Team
• Adaptability to Changing Needs/Flexibility
• Customer Focus
• Effective Communication Skills
• Interpersonal Skills

Description

We are dedicated to growing a culture of belonging through our values:
Respect | Trust | Diversity | Inclusion | Equity.

At the Department of Licensing (DOL), we recognize the importance of work life harmony and strive to create a culture where employees feel valued and respected. Our employees are trusted and encouraged to be a part of process improvements that impact their work, create value for our customers and help build trust in our government.

We are currently recruiting a data driven Quality Assurance Tester for our DRIVES/PRFT Production Support team!

As one of the most visible state agencies and the second-largest revenue generator in Washington State, we engage with over 6 million residents each year and collect nearly $3 billion in taxes and fees. We understand that our services are vital to the daily lives of our customers, enabling them to live, work, drive, and thrive. We take this responsibility to heart and are dedicated to providing equitable and meaningful access to our services for every resident.

If you are passionate about delivering high-quality testing services by establishing and executing reliable IT systems, read on!

Duties

As an entry-level Quality Assurance Tester, your technical skills will be vital for our software testing efforts, ensuring our systems run smoothly and meet all necessary standards. You'll play a key role in supporting platforms that facilitate data sharing among a wide range of partners, citizens, businesses, and government agencies. In this role, your knack for detail and dedication to data accuracy will be essential for public safety and will influence important decisions made by our agency, law enforcement, the courts, employers, and insurance companies. You will be relied upon to translate observations into clear, reproducible defect reports and to proactively probe systems for edge cases and performance issues.

Some of what you will do:
• Assist in reviewing test plans and documentation. Helping identify potential gaps or areas of improvement in these plans pre-testing.
• Develop test scenarios based on specifications and requirements, ensuring all critical features of DOL systems are thoroughly tested. Performing system, regression, and exploratory testing to identify issues early on.
• Testing, including finding and logging defects in a clear and reproducible manner. Providing detailed descriptions, steps to reproduce, and severity assessments, ensuring that all issues are communicated effectively to the development team.
• Work closely with developers, business analysts, and lead testers to clarify requirements and contribute to testing efforts. Train on and work to troubleshoot issues and suggest areas for improvement in system design or implementation.
• Help validate features, updates, or fixes meet requirements and specifications before they are deployed to production. This includes ensuring software integrates smoothly with existing systems and meets the necessary performance benchmarks.
• Participate in release testing by preparing and executing tests on software before it’s deployed to the production environment. Ensuring that all critical issues are identified and that quality standards are met.

Qualifications

What you will bring:
• Four (4) years of information technology experience such as consulting, analyzing, designing, programming, testing, maintaining software applications, or supporting software development projects.

OR
• Three (3) years of experience in application and system testing.

AND
• The ability to understand and follow agency values of respect, trust, diversity, equity and inclusion through behaviors and decisions.

Experience can be obtained concurrently.

Up to two (2) years of relevant education may substitute year for year for experience.

What may set you apart:
• Business knowledge of:
• Prorate Fuel Tax
• Drivers Licensing
• Vehicle and Vessel Licensing
• Experience implementing, designing, or testing an Enterprise COTS solution.
• Software and Application Testing Certificate of training completion.
• Testing Certification can include:
• Quality Assurance Institute (QAI).
• American Society for Quality (ASQ).
• International Software Testing Qualifications Board (ISTQB).
• International Institute for Software Testing (IIST).
• Familiarity with Visual Studio Team System (VSTS), Microsoft Test Manager (MTM) and other software test tools.
• Experience with Agile and Dev Ops methodology.
• An Associate or Bachelor degree in any subject, but preferably in a subject related to Information Technology.
• Yellow or Green Belt certification as a Lean consultant.

Additional Conditions of employment:
• This position is based in Olympia, Washington, and will require scheduled and ad hoc in-office attendance to fulfill business needs.
• Prior to a new hire, a pre-employment screening, including criminal record history, will be conducted. Information from the pre-employment check will not necessarily preclude employment but will be considered in determining the applicant’s suitability and competence to perform in the position.

Job Description

Boeing Defense Space and Security is seeking a Systems Engineer (Entry and Associate) to support Requirements, Verification and Integration efforts for next generation air refueling applications in the Puget Sound area in support of major development programs. The position provides an opportunity to work with an experienced, interdisciplinary team to develop unique systems to meet challenging requirements on air refueling development programs. This position will be based in Everett, WA.

As part of Boeing’s Defense, Space & Security organization, you will play a critical role in the integration, test, and operation of the KC-46A Pegasus, the U.S. Air Force’s next-generation aerial refueling and mobility aircraft. You will work across multi-disciplinary teams to ensure that the aircraft’s complex systems—including aerial refueling, avionics, flight controls, communications, and mission systems—are successfully integrated, tested, and delivered to the warfighter.

This position provides a unique opportunity to combine systems engineering discipline, airplane systems knowledge, and hands-on integration/test operations, directly supporting Boeing’s mission to enable global reach for the U.S. and allied forces.

Position Responsibilities
• Support airplane-level and system-level integration of hardware and software for KC-46 mission and refueling systems.
• Collaborate with cross-functional teams to develop new requirements and maintain existing requirements database.
• Coordinate verification and validation efforts across multiple development projects to enable first time quality for Integrated Product Teams and customers.
• Apply knowledge of airplane systems (avionics, refueling systems, electrical power, hydraulics, environmental controls, and flight controls) to support design, integration, and troubleshooting.
• Serve on test and operations consoles during lab, ground, and flight test events.
• Support troubleshooting, root cause analysis, and corrective action for system integration issues.
• Collaborate with avionics, communications, refueling systems, flight controls, and mission systems engineering teams to ensure seamless cross-system integration.
• Provide input to design reviews, safety reviews, and certification activities.
• Communicate effectively with engineering teams, program management, customers, and leadership through clear technical writing, presentations, and real-time decision-making.

Basic Qualifications
• Bachelor’s degree or higher in in Systems Engineering, Aerospace Engineering or related fields of studies
• Minimum of 2 years of experience in systems engineering, integration, verification, validation, or test.
• Experience with aircraft systems, avionics, or mission systems integration.
• Strong written and verbal communication skills; demonstrated ability to lead technical discussions.

This position requires the ability to obtain a US Security Clearance for which the US Government requires US Citizenship. An interim and/or final U.S. Secret Clearance Post-Start is required.

This is a 100% onsite position

Preferred Qualifications
• Experience with military aircraft development, integration, or sustainment.
• 5+ years of experience in systems engineering, integration, verification, validation, or test.
• Knowledge of air-to-air refueling systems.
• Understanding of systems safety, reliability, and airworthiness certification processes.
• Familiarity with lab integration environments (HIL/SIL) and simulation-based test.
• Current/previous DoD Secret clearance or ability to obtain.
• Familiarity with requirements management tools (DOORS or equivalent).
• Working knowledge of model based systems engineering concepts and practices (e.g. SysML, Cameo)
• USAF Tankers programmatic or operational experience.

Examines security infrastructure for radios, phones, applications, and information technology systems

About the role:

The Data Center Maintenance Technician is responsible for maintaining the cleanliness and peak performance of heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) systems within the data center facility. This role is essential in ensuring stable environmental conditions that support seamless data center operations. Technicians will work outdoors in all weather conditions and must be self-motivated, proactive, and effective team players. In addition to HVAC maintenance, technicians may be assigned other duties as needed.


What you will be doing:

HVAC Equipment Cleaning:

  1. Perform comprehensive cleaning of HVAC systems, including air handling units, ductwork, filters, coils, fans, and condensers.
  2. Utilize industry-standard cleaning techniques, tools, and materials to effectively remove dust, debris, and contaminants, optimizing system performance and efficiency.

Filter Replacement:

  1. Replace air filters according to scheduled maintenance plans to maintain optimal air quality and system functionality.
  2. Keep detailed records of filter replacements and manage an inventory of spare filters to ensure timely replacements.

Condenser and Coil Maintenance:

  1. Inspect and clean condenser coils to improve air conditioning efficiency and prevent performance degradation.
  2. Conduct routine maintenance on evaporator and condenser coils to mitigate issues related to dirt accumulation and airflow obstruction.

Ventilation System Maintenance:

  1. Maintain and clean ventilation components, including ductwork and exhaust systems, to ensure unimpeded airflow.
  2. Regularly inspect ventilation systems to prevent obstructions and optimize temperature control and air circulation.

Documentation and Reporting:

  1. Maintain accurate logs of HVAC maintenance activities, including schedules, tasks performed, and system inspections.
  2. Generate detailed reports to track HVAC equipment status, maintenance history, and compliance with operational protocols.

Collaboration and Support:

  1. Work closely with data center operations teams to align HVAC maintenance efforts with environmental and operational requirements.
  2. Assist with HVAC system installations, upgrades, and related infrastructure projects to ensure seamless integration and functionality.

Safety and Compliance:

  1. Follow all safety protocols and best practices, including the proper handling of HVAC equipment and the use of personal protective equipment (PPE).
  2. Foster a culture of safety within the data center environment by promptly identifying and reporting any potential hazards or safety concerns.


Essential Functions:

  1. Interface with technology and operate digital tools.
  2. Flexibility to work shifts, including weekends and holidays, as required.
  3. Physical fitness to perform tasks that may involve lifting, moving, and reaching HVAC equipment.
  4. Ability to stoop, stand, walk, climb stairs and ladders.
  5. Ability to lift and/or carry heavy loads of 50 lbs. or more.
  6. Adhere to Company information security policies and standards by safeguarding confidential data, protecting access credentials, completing all required trainings on time, and taking immediate action to report potential security threats or breaches.
  7. Ability to work independently with minimal instruction


Minimum Qualifications and Competencies:

  1. Requires basic knowledge of hand tools.
  2. High School Diploma
  3. Ability to comprehend and interpret instructions.
  4. Attention to detail and meticulous cleaning and maintenance of HVAC equipment.
  5. Effective communication skills for reporting findings and collaborating with team members.
  6. Willingness to learn and adapt to data center-specific HVAC cleaning and maintenance procedures.
  7. Aptitude and willingness to learn and utilize AI tools and technology.

The Boeing Library Services (BLS) team helps employees’ access, organize, analyze, manage, and distribute information. BLS optimizes the latest developments in information management strategies to support Boeing digital innovation and competitiveness, delivering high-quality, cost-effective solutions across the global enterprise.

The BLS team works with business partners across the enterprise ensuring that the right information gets to the right people at the right time to maximize the value proposition to support Boeing customers. As experts in business and technical information management, BLS employees ensure the proper management of information through the information lifecycle. This role will provide guidance and support in the proper identification, marking, cataloging, management and evaluation of critical Boeing information to support business goals across the enterprise. This role will support the databases, systems and servers responsible for the library platform. This role will direct actions and assist in creating metadata that adheres to information science standards to discover information as a strategic asset. This role will take a lead role in record auditing and ensure ongoing GTC compliance.

A successful candidate will display leadership qualities as well as a high degree of integrity, motivation, discipline, energy, and attention resulting in solutions-oriented thinking, communication, collaboration and problem-solving skills. The ideal candidate is a highly entrepreneurial self-starter and able to operate independently in a dynamic environment.

• Provides detailed guidance to end users in accessing and utilizing Boeing information properly to meet information security and protection guidelines
• Provides general guidance to end users on proper use of externally available information Boeing is contracted to utilize
• Applies metadata management principles such as authority control, classification schemes, and indexing using a specialized controlled vocabulary in support of daily cataloging activities
• Displays knowledge of current technology trends in information/metadata management systems and applications
• Demonstrates ability to work individually and collaboratively within a diverse and changing environment
